XCIV. Nos Witko et Hoygerius fratres de Lanestein et domini in Nouo Castro et in Wistritz ad vniuersorum tam praesentium quam futu- rorum notitiam volumus deuenire, quod nos bona deliberatione maturoque consilio prehabito deligenti pure propter dominum et ¡n remedium praedecessorum nostrorum monasterium seu claustrum Altouadum, vulgariter nuncupatum Wisnowibrod, donum telonis (sic), quod in ciuitate nostra videlicet in Nouo Castro nos vel aliquem no mine nostro contingit recipere, quantum ipsum monasterium tangit, duntaxat facimus liberum penitus et solutum, promittentes pro nobis heredibus et successoribus nostris et pro illis, qui ipsum telonium nostro nomine habuerint vel tenuerint pro illo vel aliis, ab ipso mo nasterio telonium a data presentium nunquam exposcere seu repetere temporibus duraturis. In cuius rei testimonium et perpetui roboris iirmamentum sigilla nostra presentibus duximus appendenda. Datum in Lucouia 4U die mensis Februarii anno domini 1349. Valorem vero qui dictas quinquaginta sex sexage- nas excrescit, in remedium anime mee et omnium meorum predeces- sorum dicto monasterio et fratribus pie largiendo promittens bona et sincera fide fraude et dolo remotis vna cum fideiussoribus meis Chwalone de Swietlik et Petro de Sestow prefatam villam cum per tinenciis suis vniuersis qualibet remota postergacione contra quam- libet personam, cuiuscumque status fuerit, iure terre iuxta regni Bohemie approbatam et hactenus obseruatam consuetudinem disbri- gare; quod si quoquo modo facere neglexerimus, obstagium debitum 07 in ciuitate Chrumpnaw dominorum de Rosenberch ad hospitem per dominum abbatem vel conuentum predictos nobis deputatum tene- bimur in personis propriis obseruare, quousque per nos antedicta villa ipsis sufficienter fuerit disbrigata. entries.english:
4 February 1349, Lucouia. The brothers Witko and Hoyer von Landstein grant Hohenfurt monastery exemption from tolls at Gratzen.

We, Witko and Hoygerius, brothers de Lanestein and lords in Nouo Castro and Wistritz, wish it to come to the knowledge of all, present and future, that after careful deliberation and mature counsel, purely for the Lord's sake and for the remedy of our predecessors' souls, we make the monastery or cloister of Altouadum, commonly called Wisnowibrod, entirely free and exempt from the toll which we or anyone in our name may receive in our town of Nouo Castro, so far as it concerns the monastery. We promise for ourselves, our heirs and successors and those who have or hold that toll in our name, for that toll or others, never to demand or claim toll from the monastery from the date of these presents, for all time. In testimony and perpetual confirmation we have had our seals attached. Given at Lucouia on 4 February in the year of the Lord 1349. From a copy in the Liber ruber privilegiorum.

21 May 1349, Krumau. Nikolaus von Swietlik sells the village of Oggold to Abbot Thomas and the convent of Hohenfurt for 56 Schock of Prague groschen.

I, Nicolaus de Swietlik, acknowledge by these presents to all that, after careful deliberation and the mature counsel and consent of my friends, I have lawfully and reasonably sold my village called Okol, containing four hides, which I had bought from my brothers Leonhard and Jesko de Swietlik for seventy Schock, to the reverend Herr Thomas, abbot, and the whole convent of Altovado for fifty-six Schock of Prague groschen, which I acknowledge receiving from them fully and entirely. The sale includes cultivated and uncultivated fields, meadows, pastures, mountains, plains, woods, thickets, waters and watercourses, rents, lordship and ownership, and all other appurtenances and revenues now there or that may arise in future, of whatever kind or name. I piously give the monastery and brothers the value exceeding the fifty-six Schock for the remedy of my soul and those of all my predecessors.

In good and sincere faith, without fraud or deceit, I promise with my sureties Chwalon de Swietlik and Peter de Sestow to clear and defend the village and all its appurtenances, without delay, against anyone of whatever status under the approved and hitherto observed custom of the kingdom of Bohemia. If we neglect to do so in any way, we shall be bound to perform the required surety service in person in the town of Chrumpnaw of the lords de Rosenberg, at a lodging appointed by the abbot or convent, until we have sufficiently cleared the village for them. In testimony I have attached my seal and that of my brother Leonhard de Swietlik. I, the aforesaid Leonhard, also attest and acknowledge these things and have attached my seal as clear testimony. Given at Chrumpnaw on the Ascension of the Lord, in 1349.

Two small white-wax seals hang from parchment strips. The first shows a helmet with a long-beaked bird as crest, inscribed “S. Nicolai de Swietlik”; the second a helmet with a cock as crest, inscribed “S. Leonhardi de Swietlik.”
